root_cause.text: The mtk_eth_soc driver directly freed metadata_dst objects using kfree() via metadata_dst_free() without respecting RCU grace periods, causing use-after-free when skbs holding non-refcounted pointers to the dst (set via skb_dst_set_noref()) were still in flight during driver teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `metadata_dst_free(eth->dsa_meta[i])` with `dst_release(&eth->dsa_meta[i]->dst)` in mtk_free_dev(). The CVE description explicitly states that metadata_dst_free() "frees the metadata_dst with kfree() immediately, bypassing the RCU grace period," while dst_release() "properly goes through the refcount path" and "schedules the actual free via call_rcu_hurry(), ensuring all RCU readers have completed before the memory is freed." The vulnerability was introduced in commit 2d7605a72906 which enabled hardware DSA untagging, creating the scenario where skbs hold non-refcounted pointers to the metadata_dst that require RCU protection.

Instead of calling the higher-level metadata_dst_free() function, it now directly calls dst_release() on the embedded dst member of the metadata structure. bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the vulnerable pattern described in the root cause. In mtk_open(), metadata_dst objects are allocated and stored in eth->dsa_meta[i] (lines 3019-3027). These objects are then used in mtk_poll_rx() where skb_dst_set_noref() is called to set non-refcounted pointers to the dst (line 1952: 'skb_dst_set_noref(skb, &eth->dsa_meta[port]->dst)'). Later, in mtk_free_dev(), these metadata_dst objects are freed using metadata_dst_free() (lines 3587-3591) without any RCU synchronization. This creates a use-after-free vulnerability because skbs with non-refcounted pointers set via skb_dst_set_noref() may still be in flight during driver teardown, but the underlying dst objects are freed immediately without waiting for RCU grace periods. The fix would require using metadata_dst_free_rcu() or calling synchronize_rcu() before freeing, neither of which is present in this commit.
